subject: ACME RFP: inference egress model, zone segmentation, and attack-surface Q&A
messages:
From: Linda Chu <linda.chu@acmefs.com>
To: jasmine_liu@redwood.com; neha_kapoor@redwood.com
Cc: john.patel@acmefs.com; security-reqs@acmefs.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: ACME RFP: clarification on egress controls and segmentation

Hi Jasmine / Neha,

Thanks for the RFI packet — we reviewed and have a few targeted technical clarifications before we finalize scoring. Our security team wants concise, diagram-backed answers to these items for the network / topology section:

1) How does Redwood prevent unintended egress of customer data from inference nodes (both hosted and Dedicated)? We want to understand control points (NAT, egress gateways, private link, customer-managed NAT IPs).
2) For Private deployments (VPC/on-prem), what network boundaries exist between tenants and between control plane and data plane? Provide a short summary of isolation primitives and typical CIDR/peering patterns.
3) Are there any runtime components that make outbound connections to third-party telemetry or package repositories? If so, can these be restricted to allow-list endpoints or run in fully air-gapped mode?

We need diagrams that can be embedded in our risk memo (png/pdf). I attached the latest ACME_RFP_v2.pdf with the RFP items highlighted. Can you send back a brief narrative + diagram and call-outs we can copy into our report?

Goal: include your answers in our security review packet by 2027-04-08.

Best,
Linda Chu
Director, Information Security
Acme Financial Services

Attachment: ACME_RFP_v2.pdf (application/pdf)

From: jasmine_liu@redwood.com
To: Linda Chu <linda.chu@acmefs.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com; marcus_lin@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME RFP: clarification on egress controls and segmentation

Hi Linda — thanks for the clear list. Quick summary below; attached is a topology diagram (redwood-egress-diagram.pdf) and a short matrix you can paste into your packet. If you want, we can turn this into a one-page diagram with call-outs tailored to ACME's cloud layout.

TL;DR answers
- Unintended egress: prevented by per-tenant egress policies + customer-managed NAT or static egress IPs; traffic leaving inference workers traverses configurable egress gateways and can be restricted to allow-list destinations.
- Private deployments: strong separation between control plane (Redwood-managed control services) and data plane (customer-hosted inference nodes); the data plane never uses Redwood-managed public internet for inference payloads unless customer config enables outbound integrations.
- Third-party outbound connections: optional and configurable; telemetry and package fetches can be disabled for air-gapped installs.

Detailed points (for your report)
1) Egress controls (hosted & Dedicated)\- By default we terminate outbound traffic from inference workers through a tenant-scoped egress gateway. For Hosted API we provide two options: (a) Redwood-managed egress with a documented set of allow-list endpoints and static IP ranges; or (b) customer-configured egress via VPC peering / PrivateLink so that outbound flows egress through customer NAT.
\- For Dedicated capacity, all inference worker egress can be routed through your dedicated NAT or a managed customer IP pool. We support SNAT with static IPs for allow-listing.
\- Additional controls: per-route egress policies, DNS filtering (via policy), TLS inspection hooks (customer-managed), and selective proxying for external calls (optional).

2) Private (VPC / on-prem) isolation model\- Control plane vs data plane: Redwood's control plane is logically separate; control-plane traffic is limited to control APIs (deployment management, metrics ingestion) over mutually authenticated mTLS. The data plane (inference nodes) is deployed inside customer VPCs or on-prem racks and does not share tenant workloads with other customers.
\- Network primitives: tenant VPC, subnet-fenced worker pools, security groups / NSGs per pool. Typical recommended pattern: dedicate a private subnet per workload class (inference, batch, admin). Where peering/PrivateLink is used, we recommend route tables that prevent direct cross-tenant routing.
\- Egress patterns: default to customer-managed egress for Private installs. For hosted Dedicated we support customer-controlled NAT or Redwood-managed gateways with SNI/DNS allow-lists.

3) Outbound dependencies / telemetry\- The runtime includes optional metrics/telemetry exports (Prometheus-compatible push gateways) and package/weight fetch from configurable object stores. All outbound destinations are configurable and can be limited to list of IPs/domains you provide. In fully air-gapped deployments we disable telemetry and package auto-fetch and provide offline bundle options.

Attachments included: redwood-egress-diagram.pdf (PDF, simplified topology) and RFI_answers_acme_april2027.xlsx (detailed mapping).

Next steps: if you confirm the level of granularity required, Neha can provide the CIDR-level example templates and Marcus can add a short threat-model callout for the RFP appendix.

Regards,
Jasmine Liu
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-egress-diagram.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Linda Chu <linda.chu@acmefs.com>
Cc: jasmine_liu@redwood.com; marcus_lin@redwood.com; karthik_iyer@redwood.com
Date: Mon, 5 Apr 2027 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: ACME RFP: clarification on egress controls and segmentation

Hi Linda — adding the technical clarifications Marcus and I discussed that you can paste into the security appendix. I included some attack-surface notes and recommended configuration snippets.

A) CIDR / peering examples (non-normative)\- Customer VPC: 10.10.0.0/16\- Worker subnet (inference): 10.10.32.0/21\- Admin/ops subnet: 10.10.40.0/24\- Redwood-managed control-plane endpoint (if used): 172.31.100.0/28 (mTLS, not in data plane)

B) Cross-tenant isolation controls\- In hosted Dedicated, inference workers run in tenant-isolated pools (no shared instance host for inference processes). We enforce Linux-level namespaces + process isolation and kernel hardening. Network paths are enforced via security groups and gateway rules to prevent east-west traffic between tenant pools.

C) KV cache and sidecar egress considerations\- KV cache shards are local to worker pools and never egress model input tokens outside configured paths. Sidecar processes that perform model-loading or metrics export are restricted by egress ACLs and run with least privilege. For extra assurance, enable prefix caching with local disk-backed caches and disable remote cache warm-up.

D) Threat-model points to include for your report (short)\- Threat: data exfil via outbound integration\-> Mitigations: allow-listing, customer-managed NAT, per-route egress policy, telemetry opt-out.\- Threat: supply-chain (package fetch) compromise\-> Mitigations: signed artifact bundles, offline weight import, restricted package repositories.

If you want exact JSON snippets of the allow-list ACLs or example iptables rules for your ops, we can provide those as an addendum.

Cheers,
Neha Kapoor
Principal Infrastructure Security Engineer | Redwood Inference

Jasmine / Neha — this is great, thank you. The diagram and the CIDR examples are exactly what our reviewers wanted. A couple of quick asks before we close the packet:

1) Can you attach a short (1-2 paragraph) statement on the telemetry-off mode that we can paste into the RFP? We prefer a committed line we can quote in the security appendix.
2) Please confirm the static IP ranges you publish for Redwood-managed egress (if we choose that path) — we need the CIDR block(s) for our firewall rules.

If you can drop those two items by EOD Thu 2027-04-08 we will include them and proceed to vendor scoring. Also CC: procurement (John) for next steps.

Best,
Linda
